engagement_title: Evergreen Provisions first apparel capsule: recover six hand painted crest panels into per ink plate art, prove them at the width they actually print on the garments the shop actually stocks, and hand the decorator a live spec run
vertical: Cannabis retail and dispensary lifestyle merchandise, two owned storefronts, Bend, Oregon, short run counter sold apparel capsule
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork apparel capsule post quoted in this line's ledger grounding_note, from a vertically integrated cannabis retailer asking for 'a production-ready apparel design system for a branded retail capsule' that 'hands cleanly to manufacturers and decorators (vectors, tech packs)', in an 'elevated streetwear' direction, on palette with no rework. The real post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional dispensary Evergreen Provisions (a generic dictionary pairing, no trademark collision), and the post's stated purple and black palette is dropped along with its from scratch garment art and embroidery digitising, which the ledger's own triage concedes are not connector work. What survives is the half that client genuinely needed and could not get: a decorator will not quote from a photograph, so the commission is recovery of the artwork that already exists into per ink plate art, plus the spec the shop floor actually works from. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that the honest fuller commission rather than a thin one, because an ink level trace off photographed painted collateral recovers real artwork, HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes for the separation sheets and the teaser set, and the InDesign convert and merge chain turns the decorator's own last season spec card PDF into a live per design run. Verdict STRENGTHEN honoured: the concept and the six item collateral set are kept intact and the depth is raised from what sat on one vector surface to five honestly counted ones.
client_one_liner: We had six crest panels hand painted for our shop walls, the painter moved away and left us nothing but photographs of them, and our screen printer will not quote a tee run off a photograph.
client_brief:
Evergreen Provisions, first apparel capsule

We run two dispensary shops in Bend, Oregon. Two years ago we paid a local sign painter to hand paint six crest panels for the walls, one for each of our house strain families. Customers photograph them constantly and ask where they can buy them. So we want a small capsule off the back of that: three tees and two hoodies, short run, sold over our own counters.

Where we are. The painter finished the panels, was paid, and moved to Montana. We do not have her sketches and there is no file of any kind. What we have is a set of photographs of the finished panels sitting on our bench, taken over two visits, and photographs of the actual blank tees and hoodies we stock, shot on the counter under our shop lights.

What we need. Our screen printer will not quote from a photograph. He needs proper artwork, one piece of art per ink, so he can burn screens off it. He also needs to know how many inks each design costs him and in what order they lay down. Last season he sent us a spec card for a different job and asked us to use the same card again so his floor recognises it, and we still have that PDF. We have a sheet listing the designs, which garment and colour each goes on, where it sits and how wide it prints.

We want to see it before we commit. A board showing each design on the actual garment colour it goes on, at the size it actually prints, plus a set of square posts for our socials that we can edit ourselves when the drop date moves.

The look. These are hand painted panels and that is the entire reason anyone wants them. Keep the brush in it. Do not turn them into flat corporate logos. Tees are thirty two dollars, hoodies seventy, and our buyer is twenty five to forty five and buys craft.

And tell us plainly what came back and what did not.
price_band_and_audience: Craft dispensary lifestyle capsule at 32 dollars a tee and 70 dollars a hoodie, buyer 25 to 45, bought at the counter on the strength of the wall panels they already photograph. The band is load bearing. At this price the painted origin is the product, so the plates have to retain brush edge, dry brush breakup and a halftoned paint field, and the palette stays earthy and limited to the inks the decorator already keeps on his shelf. Flatten those crests into clean geometric marks with a mass retail two ink treatment and the capsule reads as gas station merch, which will not hold 70 dollars. Push the other way into a foiled, sparse, monogrammed designer drop look and it misprices a counter sold 32 dollar tee and stops looking like the panels on the wall, which is the only reason the customer walked over. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every plate separates correctly. A real posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A vertically integrated cannabis retailer running two dispensary storefronts, launching a short-run counter-sold apparel capsule.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2019, Bend, Oregon. Two owned dispensary shops, owner-run, with a small counter-retail apparel line.
brand_identity.about: Evergreen Provisions runs two dispensary shops in Bend, built around six house strain families. Two years ago the owners paid a local sign painter to hand-paint a crest panel for each family onto the shop walls. Customers photograph them constantly and ask where they can buy them, and the first apparel capsule exists to answer that question without losing the hand that made the panels.
brand_identity.audience: Craft-minded dispensary customers aged 25 to 45 who buy at the counter on the strength of the wall panels they already photograph. People who pay for the painted origin, not for a logo.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Tees at 32 dollars, hoodies at 70 dollars, short-run and counter-sold. Elevated streetwear priced above gas-station merch and below a designer drop. The painted texture is the product, so the value sits in the brush surviving, not in gloss or foil.
brand_identity.typography: Display in a painted or brushed-character face that echoes the sign painter's hand, kept legible. Support and spec type in a plain workhorse sans so the plates and sheets read cleanly. Type never competes with the painted crest.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, plain-spoken, shop-floor honest. No luxury posturing and no carnival hype. Example line: "These are hand painted panels and that is the entire reason anyone wants them. Keep the brush in it, and tell us plainly what came back and what did not."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The six crest panels were hand-painted by a local sign painter who has since moved to Montana and left no sketches or files. The only surviving artwork is a set of bench photographs of the finished panels, shot over two visits under mixed light. There is no vector art and no separation art, which is exactly why the screen printer cannot quote a run.
brand_identity.values: Craft and honesty. Keep the painted hand, hold the palette to the inks the decorator already stocks, and say plainly what the paintings can and cannot give a screen.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_crest_panels/ (6 frames, roughly 4200 x 4200)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photographs of six hand painted crest panels on primed board, taken on the shop bench across two separate visits under mixed daylight and counter light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The six panels as they hang on the wall. Two were shot on a different day so they sit a little different."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six are compound lockups, a ring of painted lettering around a central sprig, and a single compound selection returns the ring and the outer arcs while silently dropping the sprig at full success. One panel is painted in a deep aubergine that sits within a hair of the stained board behind it, so an ink level selection there has almost no contrast to work with, and the dry brush hairlines and the small painted caps are barely open in the paint itself, so whether they survive a trace is a property of each panel rather than of the tracing.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_garment_blanks/ (5 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs of the actual blanks the shop stocks: three tees (bone, heather olive, black) and two hoodies (black, oat), laid on the counter.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The blanks we carry, shot on the counter so you can see the real colours."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: They were shot under warm counter lights, so the black hoodie photographs brown and the heather olive reads yellow, which makes every judgement about ink contrast on those grounds wrong until the frames are corrected. One of the five was shot on a hanger rather than flat and sits noticeably off level.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_spec_card_2024.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The decorator's own spec card artwork from last season's run, supplied as the press PDF his floor already recognises: job name, ink list, plate order, placement and print width.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer wants us to use. Same layout as last year, he says just fill it in."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card's four blocks read as visually separate on the printed page but the PDF's text is one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes a frame granularity nothing like the printed page suggests. The mapping readout also omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past it is short, and the validator still reports the mapping valid.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_plate_schedule.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Six rows written by the shop: design name, garment, garment colour, placement, print width in inches, and the ink count as the shop guessed it.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Designs, garments, placements and the widths our printer gave us over the phone."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: One row is a sleeve hit at a print width a small fraction of the chest widths, and two rows name the same crest on two different garment colours, which is one design and two plate sets rather than two designs. The ink counts are the shop's guesses and are not derived from the art.

assets_supplied.name: evergreen_ink_book.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text list of the stock inks the decorator keeps on his shelf, with the shop's own notes on which ones they like.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The inks he already has. Anything off this list costs us a mixing charge."

acceptance_bar: Every plate is a separate piece of single ink geometry that a decorator could burn a screen from. A sheet showing a picture of a separation is not a separation.
Every delivered vector carries a real viewBox and no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and drops onto a coloured garment ground without a box behind it.

At the print width the schedule states, on the garment colour that design actually prints on, each crest keeps its hairlines and its counters stay open. Judged at reproduction size on the real ground, never at canvas scale.
The one colour reductions for the dark garments are a genuine redraw of value, not the colour art with its colour taken away.
The six panels read as one capsule palette, not as six paintings shot on two different days. A panel that cannot be brought to the set is named rather than shipped at eighty percent.
The blanks are corrected to their honest colours before any ink contrast decision is made against them, and the correction is stated.
No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no returned tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.

The design list is reconciled before anything is counted: the spec card run has one card per real design, every declared field lands on every card, and the reconciliation is stated rather than assumed.
On the separation sheets every plate is separately readable, including where plates overlap. A sheet where the top plate hides the ones beneath it fails even if it exported successfully.
The mockup board shows each design at true relative scale on its blank, not scaled to fill the garment.
The teaser set and the sheets arrive as one working file we can edit ourselves, each canvas keeping its own size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.

The note names, per design, the ink count as separated rather than as guessed, the plate order, anything that could not be recovered from the paintings, and anything the print process cannot be given.

It levels and colour corrects the panel captures to one capsule palette, corrects the blanks so their real colours can be judged, pulls each crest at ink level off a photographed painted board by naming the paint's own visual properties rather than the panel it sits on, masks and flattens each ink into its own plate BEFORE tracing, halftones the paint field at a chosen radius while the painted lettering stays crisp, builds the one colour reductions as a value redraw, knocks the blanks to a house ground for the mockup, and performs the vector hygiene the tracer does not do for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The separation sheets, the mockup board and the square teaser set as one native editable document carrying roots at more than one canvas size, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout. Every photograph must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, every crest goes in as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper so it stays editable vector and does not run off the artboard, and the payload travels as an uploaded file because inlined garment photography passes the inline threshold immediately.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign document conversion, merge template authoring and render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (both as readout and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The decorator's spec card run. His own last season press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, bound to the reconciled plate schedule, and merged one record per page so his floor gets the card it already recognises with this season's designs in it. Merged to InDesign first and rendered separately, because the merge tool silently ignores resolution and only the render step yields real print DPI proofs.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type across the separation sheets, the mockup board and the teaser set. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on a craft counter capsule rather than a corporate merch programme. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or the type falls back silently.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface

adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the shop does not have, a camera scale worn timber counter surface that the square teaser canvases sit the folded garments on, IP clean and with generative tech candidates excluded. The Boards half persists the shortlist the two owners and the decorator sign off from, placed within the twelve per call cap, with a partial success read as partial and vector understood to be unacceptable there.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The plates and reductions are raster and vector work with a production spec, the spec cards are a genuine record per page run against a template the client actually supplied, and the sheets and teasers need an authored fixed canvas document because the shop edits them next drop. Nothing else in the connector composes free form layout.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming a surface per deliverable, and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline: a manifest keyed by role so that forty artefacts later the agent still knows which URL is which panel, which blank and which schedule row.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Preview all six panels and all five blanks and triage them: which panels are single element crests and which are compound lockups, which paint runs close in value to its board, which blank is off level, and which capture belongs to which visit.
trajectory.judgement: The photographs are the only thing that can settle what each crest is actually made of. Reading the schedule tells you what the shop calls them, which is not the same question and is answered slower.
trajectory.produces: A per asset triage note covering crest structure, paint against board contrast, illuminant and tilt.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, before any crop or bounds decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Correct the five blanks so the garment colours are honest, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: Every later decision about whether an ink reads on a ground is made against these frames. Judging contrast against a black hoodie that photographs brown is judging against a garment that does not exist.
trajectory.produces: Five corrected blank masters with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Bring the six panel captures to one capsule palette, correcting each toward one target with its own call rather than one batched pass.
trajectory.judgement: One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for frames shot on two visits under two lights. The target is a set of paintings that look like one hand, not six good photographs.
trajectory.produces: Six panel masters on one palette with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Pull each crest at ink level, naming the paint's own visual properties rather than the panel it sits on, and taking compound lockups element by element rather than in one prompt.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the substrate returns the board. A compound prompt returns a plausible looking mask that has quietly lost an element, and the aubergine panel has almost nothing for a selection to hold on to.
trajectory.produces: Per crest ink level masks, composited per element where the lockup is compound, each with its returned bounding box.

trajectory.action: Set polarity, crop to each mask's own returned bounds with a little padding, and trace.
trajectory.judgement: Tracing the raw mask returns a black box with the art knocked out of it, and tracing the inverted one returns the positive. Both report success, so the polarity decision is the whole difference.
trajectory.produces: One raw traced SVG per crest.

trajectory.action: Perform the vector hygiene the tracer does not: inject a viewBox and remove the opaque full canvas ground path on every trace.
trajectory.judgement: A trace with no viewBox does not scale and a trace with its ground path intact drops a white box onto a black hoodie. Neither is reported anywhere.

trajectory.action: Build the separations: mask each ink and flatten the rest away so each plate carries one ink only, choose which crest carries a halftoned paint field and at what radius, then trace each plate.
trajectory.judgement: Separating after the trace gives a mess of near identical fills. The craft is deciding, per design, how many inks the painting is actually worth on a 32 dollar tee, and which parts of the brush are worth a halftone rather than an extra screen.
trajectory.produces: Per design plate sets, one piece of art per ink, plus the halftoned paint field plates.

trajectory.action: Build the one colour reductions for the dark garments as a value redraw rather than a desaturation, then knock the blanks to the house ground the mockup board needs.
trajectory.judgement: A desaturated colour separation collapses two inks of similar value into one grey mush. Deciding what survives when only one ink is left is the reduction.
trajectory.produces: One colour cuts per design and cut out blanks on the house ground.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own, judged against a craft counter capsule at 32 and 70 dollars. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name, and a display cut is reached by its own slug rather than by a heavy weight.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML carrying the separation sheets, the mockup board and the square teaser roots, each root declaring its own canvas size, every photograph inlined as image data, every crest and plate placed as inline SVG in an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, family and weight declared on every text element, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the artboard, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how a separation sheet shows overlapping inks so a decorator can read the trap between them.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole capsule set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export by URL, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every canvas after it.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the rest.

trajectory.action: Convert the decorator's spec card PDF, export the IDML, and read what the conversion actually exposes as editable frames and what each frame's true story text actually contains, before promising any field to any frame.
trajectory.judgement: What a printed card looks like and what its PDF converts into are unrelated questions, and the readout the mapping tool hands back is not the document. Promising a mapping before looking is promising something nobody has checked.
trajectory.produces: A real frame inventory with bounds and typography, and the reconstructed true story text per frame.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the schedule into a real design list, prepare the merge template, confirm by round trip that every field placeholder is actually present, then merge one record per page and render proofs at real print resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Two rows naming one crest on two garment colours is one design and two plate sets. A success message from the prepare step is not evidence a field landed, and the merge step ignores resolution entirely, so proofs have to come off the render.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template, a press PDF whose page count equals the reconciled design count, and print resolution proofs.

trajectory.action: License the counter surface frame, grade it into the capsule world, create the selects board and add the capsule set within the per call placement cap re sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector plates are not boardable so they belong in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the decorator does not phone back.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether these particular traces still hold at the width they actually print, on the garment colour they actually print on. The paintings carry dry brush hairlines and small painted caps whose counters are barely open in the paint itself, and the tracer takes no options at all, so the only lever is the raster prep upstream. At canvas scale every trace looks clean and complete. The sleeve hit prints at a fraction of the chest widths, and whether its counters close and its hairlines drop out at that size, against olive or against black rather than against white, is a property of that one painting meeting that one reproduction size and is not reported by anything.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the answer does not exist until the plate has been traced and laid down at its true width on the corrected garment ground, and there is no tracer parameter that would have prevented it. Nothing in the brief or the schedule states it: the schedule gives print widths because a decorator needs print widths, not as a warning about counters. It is not a propagation re run either, because the response is a different route for that design, either rebuilding the plate as a masked and flattened solid before tracing so the stroke carries weight, or accepting a coarser reduction for that placement and saying so.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster prep for the affected designs, rebuild those plates through a mask and flatten route rather than tracing the painterly stroke directly, re trace, redo the vector hygiene, and re judge every affected design at its stated width on its stated ground before any of it reaches a sheet.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A capsule where the sleeve design prints as a plugged blob and the small painted caps close up on press, discovered by the decorator after screens are burned, on a capsule whose entire premise is that the brush survived.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises the construct the separation sheets are built on. A separation sheet shows each ink as its own layer sitting over the ones beneath it so the decorator can read the overlap and the trap. Authored the natural way that is a blended or partially transparent stack, and the importer discards the blend outright and returns a plain opaque shape, at full success and with no warning of any kind. The returned per canvas markup is the only channel that reports it, and the document's own rendition returns the first artboard only, so every sheet after the first can be checked no other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is the last step of the authoring, and doing it right first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. Nothing states it: the brief asks for one piece of art per ink and says nothing about how a sheet is drawn. It is not a propagation re run, because the response is a different construction, either separating the plates spatially into registered panels with a printed offset key, or baking the overlap into a raster upstream so the trap is part of the picture rather than of the layout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re author the separation roots around whichever construction survives, re upload, re run the readiness check, re export, and audit every sheet from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Separation sheets handed to a decorator on which the top plate covers the ones beneath it, so every design appears to be a one ink job, with the export having reported success throughout.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the decorator's spec card actually is once converted, as opposed to what its printed face suggests. Its four blocks read as separate on paper, but the conversion decides the frame granularity and can collapse a continuous flow into a single frame, so there may be no separate name frame and ink frame to map fields to at all. Compounding it, the readout the mapping tool returns omits a run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed, every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, and the validator returns valid with no warnings on offsets that are wrong.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that avoids it and no parameter that controls it, because the granularity is a property of how that PDF was made and the readout's omission is invisible in the readout. Nothing states it: the client says only that the printer wants the same card again. It is not a propagation re run, because the correct response is a different mapping strategy computed from a different source of truth, the reconstructed story text from the round tripped document rather than the tool's own readout, plus a decision about which fields the exposed frames can carry at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Recompute every offset from the reconstructed story text, re prepare the template, verify by a second round trip that each field placeholder is genuinely present rather than trusting the success message, re merge, and where two blocks collapsed into one frame decide which fields move into the note instead.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A spec card run that reports success, renders the right number of pages, and reaches the decorator's floor with the ink list and the plate order silently missing from every card.

deliverables.name: Recovered Evergreen crest system
deliverables.spec: Six crests recovered from photographs of hand painted panels as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, compound lockups complete rather than missing their centre element, and each holding its hairlines and open counters at the width the schedule says it prints, on the garment colour it prints on. Delivered with the one colour reductions for the dark garments as a genuine redraw of value.

deliverables.name: Per ink plate art and garment cutouts
deliverables.spec: For every design, one piece of art per ink, each carrying a single ink's geometry and nothing else, produced by masking and flattening before tracing rather than by separating a trace afterwards, plus the halftoned paint field plates at the chosen radius with the painted lettering left crisp. Paired with the five blanks knocked to the house ground for the mockup board, alpha intact at shoulder and hem.

deliverables.name: Evergreen capsule capture set
deliverables.spec: Six panel captures brought to one capsule palette across two shooting visits, and five garment blanks corrected to their honest colours so ink contrast decisions made against them can be trusted, plus one licensed camera scale counter surface frame graded into the same world. Per frame parameter log with one line on why each frame differs from its neighbours.

deliverables.name: Decorator spec card run
deliverables.spec: The decorator's own last season card PDF reverse engineered into a live merge template and bound to the reconciled design list, delivered as one press PDF with one card per design and a page count equal to that reconciled count, every declared field present on every card, plus print resolution proofs rendered separately for sign off. The reconciliation itself is part of the deliverable, not an assumption.

deliverables.name: Capsule set as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying the separation sheets, the mockup board and the square teaser roots, each root keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the crests and plates as real vector shapes, every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, every plate separately readable on the sheets, and each design shown at true relative scale on its blank. Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half.

deliverables.name: Handover note and selects board

Paired with a persistent shareable selects board carrying the capsule set with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: Every delivered crest and plate SVG carries a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse each delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: Each design's plate set contains exactly one piece of art per declared ink, and each plate carries a single ink's geometry rather than a multi colour trace.
verifiers_auto.how: Count the distinct fills present in each plate file and count plate files per design against the reconciled schedule and the merged card content.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions, and no tradeoff record captured in the run carries an upscale entry.

verifiers_auto.text: The garment cutouts carry genuine alpha at shoulder and hem rather than a filled rectangle.

verifiers_auto.text: On every separation sheet each plate is independently present in the returned markup rather than covered by the plate above it.

verifiers_human.text: The work reads as a 32 dollar tee and 70 dollar hoodie craft capsule, not as mass retail merch and not as a designer drop.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster and vector production work, which need an authored fixed canvas document, and which belong in a genuine record per page merge against the template the client actually supplied.

Selection prompt wording on each panel: naming the board takes the board, naming the paint's own visual properties takes the ink, and a compound lockup taken in one prompt comes back plausible and incomplete.
What to do with the aubergine panel, whose paint and board sit within a hair of each other, versus naming it as the one that could not be pulled cleanly.
How many inks each painting is actually worth on a 32 dollar tee, given that the ink counts in the schedule are the shop's guesses and every extra screen is real money.
Which parts of the brush earn a halftoned paint field and at what radius, and which parts must stay crisp.
Polarity before tracing, and whether the deliverable is the two colour trace or the masked and flattened colour accurate plate, decided per design rather than once.
What survives in a one colour reduction when two inks of similar value are left with one screen between them.
Whether two rows naming one crest on two garment colours is two designs or one design with two plate sets, and how that changes the card count.
How a separation sheet shows overlapping inks so a decorator can read the trap between plates.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a craft counter capsule rather than a corporate merch programme, plus the real numeric weight per family.
Which fields the converted spec card can actually carry, once its exposed frames are known, and which move into the note instead.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns pretty crests. IDENTITY: these are one named sign painter's six actual panels, hanging on the wall of two shops, that customers already photograph. A regenerated crest is a different painting, and the entire commercial premise of the capsule is that the customer recognises the thing on the wall. SPEC: a decorator burns screens off one piece of art per ink, with correct polarity, a real viewBox, no ground rectangle and open counters at a stated print width on a stated garment colour, none of which a generated image is or can be checked for, and a press PDF whose page count equals the reconciled design count is a hard count rather than a picture. EDITABILITY: the sheets and teasers are defined by being editable, because the drop date and the featured design will move and a two person shop cannot re commission. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this trace keep its hairlines at sleeve width on black, did the plate under the top one survive the import, did the field the tool said it wrote actually land in the template.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, halftone with a mask and blackAndWhite true, monochromatic_tint, remove_background in both forms, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls. The spot plate route (mask, invert, fill, then trace) is a verified collateral unlock, the compound mark partial selection and the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry are live findings, and the missing viewBox plus the opaque path zero are documented behaviours the acceptance bar scores because no tool performs that hygiene. Vectorize takes no options at all, which is precisely why the reproduction size checkpoint can only be answered by looking. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, an image left as a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, mix-blend-mode and filter blur are DROPPED and multi layer shadow is TRUNCATED to layer one with no warning, and the rendition preview is documented as PAGE 1 ONLY, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined garment photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified headless and synchronous; the lossy textContent readout, the validator returning valid on wrong offsets, the prepare step reporting success while dropping mappings, and the frame granularity of a converted PDF being outside the author's control are all live findings; PDF merge output is one record per page in correct order; resolution is silently ignored on the merge and real DPI comes only from the render. Bleed cannot be introduced from a PDF sourced template and pdfPreset is unusable, so neither is gated and both are named in the handover. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, including the case sensitivity trap and the non standard numeric weights. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returns genuine camera scale, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no upscaling, no photo compositing tool (the mockups are separate placed elements on an authored canvas), no OCR, no text to image, no fill_text, no animate_design, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20.
